# RouterOS Provider

These are the reference docs for the
[TohaUA fork](https://github.com/TohaUA/terraform-provider-routeros).
Keep `source = "terraform-routeros/routeros"` when using fork binaries from GitHub Releases.
[Installation instructions](https://github.com/TohaUA/terraform-provider-routeros#installing-the-fork)

## Compatibility

The provider accepts **RouterOS 7.25 and later**. Acceptance CI targets **7.25.2** over native API
and REST. Individual resources may also require a specific RouterOS version, package, or hardware.
[Coverage and migration guide](guides/routeros_7_25.md)

## Getting started

Enable `www-ssl` and use `https://` for REST, or enable `api-ssl` and use `apis://` for native
API. Assign a server certificate to the service and configure the issuing CA as needed. Supply the
provider password through `ROS_PASSWORD`. Plaintext `http://` and `api://` expose credentials and
configuration on the network. [RouterOS REST API](https://manual.mikrotik.com/docs/developer-guides/rest-api/) · [RouterOS native API](https://manual.mikrotik.com/docs/developer-guides/api/)

### TLS certificate pinning

Certificate pinning is available from fork v2.5.0. To trust a specific router certificate,
set `tls_fingerprint` in the provider block or set `ROS_TLS_FINGERPRINT`.
Use `https://` or `apis://` and leave `ca_certificate` and `insecure` unset, including their
environment variables.

Compute the SHA-256 fingerprint from a trusted copy of the router's leaf certificate.

```sh
openssl x509 -in router-leaf.pem -noout -fingerprint -sha256
```

Copy the hexadecimal part after `=`. Colon separators are accepted. In pinning mode the
provider authenticates the router by matching this fingerprint in place of normal CA and
hostname checks. Before rotating the certificate, verify the replacement fingerprint through
a trusted channel and coordinate the certificate and Terraform configuration changes.

## Example usage

```terraform
terraform {
  required_providers {
    routeros = {
      source = "terraform-routeros/routeros"
    }
  }
}

provider "routeros" {
  hosturl        = "https://router.example"      # env ROS_HOSTURL
  username       = "terraform"                   # env ROS_USERNAME
  ca_certificate = "/path/to/ca/certificate.pem" # env ROS_CA_CERTIFICATE
  # Set ROS_PASSWORD in the environment instead of a literal password.
  # insecure (ROS_INSECURE) skips TLS verification (lab use only) and cannot be combined with ca_certificate.
}

resource "routeros_interface_gre" "gre_hq" {
  name           = "gre-hq-1"
  remote_address = "10.77.3.26"
  disabled       = true
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `ca_certificate` (String) Path to MikroTik's certificate authority file (env: ROS_CA_CERTIFICATE).
- `hosturl` (String) URL of the MikroTik router, default is TLS connection to REST. Required for IP/API/REST resources; optional when using only layer-2 discovery/bootstrap resources.
	* API: api[s]://host[:port]
		* api://router.local
		* apis://router.local:8729
	* REST: http[s]://host
		* http://router.local
		* https://router.local
		* router.local
		* 127.0.0.1

	Plaintext schemes (http:// and api://) send credentials and traffic unencrypted; prefer https:// or apis://.
	Standard proxy environment variables (HTTP_PROXY, HTTPS_PROXY, NO_PROXY) apply to the REST (http:// and https://) transport only; api:// and apis:// connect directly.

	export ROS_HOSTURL=router.local
- `insecure` (Boolean) Skip TLS certificate verification (not recommended) (env: ROS_INSECURE).
- `password` (String, Sensitive) Password for the MikroTik user (env: ROS_PASSWORD).
- `rest_timeout` (Number) Timeout, in seconds, for a single request to the router. Applies to both the REST and the API transport.
- `suppress_syso_del_warn` (Boolean) Suppress the system object deletion warning (env: ROS_SUPPRESS_SYSO_DEL_WARN).
- `tls_fingerprint` (String) Expected SHA-256 fingerprint (64 hex characters, optional colons or `sha256:` prefix) of the router's TLS leaf certificate. Mutually exclusive with `insecure` and `ca_certificate` (env: ROS_TLS_FINGERPRINT).
- `username` (String) Username for the MikroTik WEB/Winbox. Required for IP/API/REST resources.


	export ROS_USERNAME=admin
